title: Ambiguous or unambiguous question
decision: whether an open-domain question is ambiguous (several distinct interpretations with different answers) or has a single answer, judged from the question alone

source.name: AmbigQA (AmbigNQ): Min et al., AmbigQA: Answering Ambiguous Open-domain Questions (2020), arXiv:2004.10645
source.split: validation, configuration light (2,002 questions); test annotations are not public

notes: Derived label, not a field of the source: yes = every released annotation of the question has type multipleQAs (1,002 questions, 642 of them with one annotation), no = every annotation has type singleAnswer (830, 145 with one annotation); 170 questions whose annotations disagree on the type are dropped (787 questions have one annotation, 1,120 two, 95 three). Sample: 500 yes + 500 no (317 and 87 of them rest on one annotation; meta.annotation_types). The questions are search queries from NQ-open; the card says the ambiguities are "sometimes subtle, many of which are only apparent after examining evidence provided by a very large text corpus", so the label is hard to recover from the question alone. Text unchanged. Decontamination against the authors' training data (scan of 7 October 2026, 1,546,178 training records): 1 of 1000 items removed because a text field of the item occurs in it, and 1 more to restore the balance of the classes; 998 items remain.
